note: The donor-hardware session, as gates a script can check. Nothing here claims a run works: it checks that a captured log proves what the plan says it proves, and it refuses to score a log as hardware evidence when it cannot tell.

log_shape.active_app: \AD102-UNLOCK\RUNnnnn.TXT on the USB stick, one file per boot, never overwritten
log_shape.read_only_diagnostic: \\GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the USB stick; the VRAM-block probe build also writes one \\PROM-ssss-bb-dd-f-nnnn.BIN per card it read, named after that card and that run, never overwritten

readonly_guide.title: Read-only hardware execution guide, step by step
intro: The sections after this one describe the gates. This one is the sequence that produces a log to score, for every image in the catalogue that writes nothing to the GPU, and names the fact in each log that a hardware-dependent item is waiting for.

Every read-only and preparation run stored under `captured_runs` below was executed on this bench; **no actuating image has ever run**. Every tool in the chain prints `HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0`, and no captured log changes a row in `docs/readiness_status.json` by itself: a log is something a reviewer reads, not a flag this repository flips.
readonly_guide.naming: There is no script called `build-sign-stage` in this repository. Building, signing and staging one image is a single command with two switches: `-Only <id>` chooses the image from `docs/image_variants.json`, and `-StageDrive <letter>` copies the signed `EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI` onto the stick after a verified backup of whatever was there. `src/Build-Sign-Deploy-UniversalGPU.ps1` is that command, and `docs/BUILD_SIGN_DEPLOY.md` is its user document.

preconditions.why: the programmer, the known-good firmware image and the SPI part number are on the bench before the first boot; none of the images below writes the GPU, but the bench rule does not depend on that
serial, slot, board model and the vendor tool's VBIOS version, so the BDF and device ID in the log can be tied to a piece of silicon afterwards
no `GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-*.TXT` and no `AD102-UNLOCK\RUN*.TXT` on the stick; a stale file is indistinguishable from a live one and `session_preflight.py` refuses a medium that carries one

for every stage: the serial and slot of every card in the machine, plus the ordered BDF list the image is built with. This fork runs an ordered list with one card active at a time, so a two-card machine is the ordinary case and the list, not the card count, is what has to be written down

after each candidate, boot Windows once and record the build, driver version and device status: the read-only images promise the card is untouched, and this is the observation that would notice if it were not

the signing certificate lives in WSL (`$HOME/secureboot-signing/uefi-db.key` and `.crt`) and the same certificate must be enrolled in the BIOS `db`; the script refuses to sign when it is not, unless you pass `-SkipDbCheck` and accept a receipt that reads `DB_ENROLLED=UNKNOWN`
every command is written from the repository root, with the signed outputs landing in `artifacts\signed`

steps.title: confirm the catalogue accepts the candidate
steps.expect: one `CATALOGUE ... variants=31 families=4` line, then a `VARIANT <id> SAFETY=<class> BINARY=<name>` line per image; `NOT_BUILDABLE` lines say what this tree cannot produce and why. The candidate must be listed with the safety class in the table below.
steps.if_not: a missing id is a catalogue problem, not a bench problem: fix the tree before touching the stick.

steps.title: build, sign and stage in one command
steps.expect: `VARIANT_BEGIN` for the one image, `SIGNING_CERTIFICATE ... DB_ENROLLED=TRUE`, the verified signed SHA-256, `STAGED diag-topology-log PATH=... DRIVE=G:`, and a final `STATUS=SIGNED=1 FAILED=0 ... HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0`. A stick holds one `BOOTX64.EFI`, so this is one candidate per stick: the previous image is backed up locally before it is replaced.

expect_tokens.token: STATUS={0} SIGNED={1} FAILED={2} SKIPPED={3} DB_ENROLLED={4} HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0 MATRIX={5}

steps.if_not: `Refusing to stage` names the safety class and the missing switch. `-AcceptActuatingDeploy` exists for images that write the GPU; no read-only candidate in this guide needs it. `-SignOnly` builds and signs without touching a stick.

steps.title: check the bench before the boot
steps.expect: `STICK FREE_OF_OLD_LOGS=1`, `IMAGE ... BYTES=... SHA256=...` for the file that will actually boot, the six `MANUAL` gates, and `PREFLIGHT_VERDICT=PASS ... CHECKS=2 HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0`. `--skip-profile` is right for every candidate here: the reviewed ESP profile belongs to the waived stages. Add `--assets AD102,GA102` once the run is meant to get past `EFI_CRC_ERROR`: the image reads the five pinned files from the stick's root and hashes each before use, and a 3080 boot reads `\AD102-ASSETS\gsp_ga10x.bin` through its manifest's alternate path, so the check names that dependency instead of leaving it to a later `Pinned asset unavailable` line.
steps.if_not: `STALE_LOGS=` with an `ACTION=` line means the medium is not empty: archive and wipe it (M3) rather than rebooting over an old log. `IMAGE EMPTY=1` or `PE_HEADER=0` means step 2 did not produce the file you think it did.

steps.title: boot the stick once, from the firmware boot menu
steps.expect: Choose the USB entry once and let the image run to its own end. Do not retry inside the same session: the image takes the first free number on the medium, starting at 0000, so a second boot writes a second file and the two are only distinguishable by their numbers and their contents. The read-only candidates print `GPU hardware untouched` and return, and the handoff candidates start Windows after the log is closed.
steps.if_not: a hang is a finding: power-cycle, keep the stick as it is, and record what the screen last showed. Nothing in a read-only session writes the card, so a hang here is a firmware or console fault, not a damaged GPU.

steps.title: capture the log, then empty the medium
steps.command:
$evidence = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ('donor-evidence\' + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'))
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $evidence | Out-Null
$log = Get-ChildItem G:\ -Filter 'GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-*.TXT' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -Last 1
Copy-Item -LiteralPath $log.FullName -Destination $evidence
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 (Join-Path $evidence $log.Name)
(Get-Content -LiteralPath $log.FullName | Measure-Object -Line).Lines
steps.expect: The file named by the log's own `LOG_FILE=` line is the one to copy (the numbers start at 0000 and count up; on a clean medium the first run is `-0000.TXT`). Copy it off before wiping anything, and record its SHA-256, byte count and line count next to the candidate id. Wipe the stick afterwards so the next candidate starts from an empty medium.
steps.if_not: an empty stick with no log means the image never reached its save step. The screen said why: the last line before it stopped is the finding, and there is nothing to score.

steps.title: score the log against the gates
steps.expect: one `GATE <id> STAGE=<stage> RESULT=PASS` line per gate in the stage, the `NOTE` advisories, the six `MANUAL` gates, the `NOT_PROVEN` list, and `RUN_LOG_VERDICT=PASS ... HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0 GATES=3 GATES_FAILED=0`. Exit code `0` means every gate in that stage passed; `1` names the first failure in `FIRST_FAILED=`.
steps.if_not: exit `2` is a missing log, exit `3` is a log carrying the fixture marker (a synthetic log can never score as hardware evidence), and exit `1` is a real gate failure: `FIRST_FAILED=` names it, and the gate's own paragraph above says what it does not prove. For `prep-selected` and `dxe-prep-selected` the same command takes `--stage prepare` and the app's numbered log.

readonly_guide.after_the_steps: That is the loop: build-sign-stage, boot once, capture, score. The verdict is written into the session record beside the candidate id and the goal it was collected for. It does not change `hardware_verified` for anything, and the next section says why: a green read-only log is a statement about one image on one machine, not about a card.

candidates.title: topology with a numbered USB log
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The baseline read-only contact: PCI tree, GPU identities, GOP and console ownership, one numbered log. This is the image the R1-R3 gates were written for.

evidence.token: TOPOLOGY_VERDICT=%s NVIDIA_CONOUT_BLOCKER=%u
evidence.why: names the configured-console finding on the machine in front of you: whether an AMD display function owns the console, or an NVIDIA path is configured and blocks it

evidence.token: ERROR_CONSOLE_ISOLATION=%s
evidence.why: the error-console half of the same question: an independent AMD `ErrOut` observation is what a console-handover refactor would rest on

evidence.token: GPU[%zu] BDF=%04x:%02x:%02x.%u ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x PCI_INDEX=%zu PARENT=%zu ROOT_PORT=%zu DEPTH=%u ANCESTRY=%u ROOT_VALID=%u GOP_COUNT=%u
evidence.why: one line per GPU with its GOP count, so the surviving-non-target-GOP question B2 is about is answered for this cabling instead of assumed

evidence.token: LOG_FILE=\\GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-%04u.TXT
evidence.why: a numbered log written by an image launched from USB is the writable-medium half of B9 observed rather than assumed

evidence.token: PCI[%zu] %04x:%02x:%02x.%u %04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x CLASS=%04x ROOTPORT=%u PRIMARY=%02x BUSWINDOW=%02x-%02x BY_DRIVER=%u KNOWN=%u AGENT=%p PATH=%zu
evidence.why: device and subsystem id of every PCI node: the identity row a per-SKU entry (AD104/AD106/AD107, other GA102 ids) starts from

candidates.does_not_prove: that the card can be detached, unlocked or flashed: every eligibility flag in the log is zero by construction, and the report ends with `GPU hardware untouched`.

candidates.title: topology with a log and automatic Windows handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The same report, then the explicitly pinned Windows Boot Manager. The added value is not the topology: it is the observation that the reviewed ESP GUID boots Windows on this machine, after the log is closed.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID, and the image states it neither resets nor rewrites BootOrder

evidence.token: Starting the explicitly pinned Windows Boot Manager directly.
evidence.why: the line that must be followed by a Windows boot: the reviewed GUID is right only if Windows actually starts

evidence.token: SAVE_LOG_STATUS=%#llx ROTATING_FILE=GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-NNNN.TXT
evidence.why: the log is durably written before the handoff begins, so a failed handoff still leaves the evidence

candidates.does_not_prove: that the GUID names the only Windows loader, or that BitLocker, Secure Boot policy or anti-cheat accept that path (E10); it shows one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: selected-GPU observation with a log
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The passive diagnostic with an ordered selection: one snapshot, every requested BDF resolved before any report, then per-target identity and a summary. This is the read-only image that says something about two cards.

evidence.token: PASSIVE_SELECTION=GPU_IDENTIFIED TARGET=%04x:%02x:%02x.%u ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x CLASS=%04x
evidence.why: the requested BDF resolved to a device and subsystem id from the live snapshot: the runtime selector's positive case on real handles

evidence.token: SELECTION_SEQUENCE=REFUSED CODE=%d COMPLETED=0 REQUESTED=%u TOPOLOGY_VERDICT=%d
evidence.why: a wrong or absent BDF refuses the whole sequence with no partial selection: the negative half of the same feature

evidence.token: SELECTION_STEP[%zu]=PASSIVE_IDENTIFIED ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x CLASS=%04x ROOT_INDEX=%zu DEPTH=%u GOP_COUNT=%u BY_DRIVER=%u OPENERS_KNOWN=%u
evidence.why: one numbered report per selected card in order, with its own GOP count and driver-owner status: the per-card data a multi-GPU refactor has to be written against

evidence.token: SELECTION_SEQUENCE=PASSIVE_IDENTIFIED COMPLETED=%u NON_SELECTED_NVIDIA_COUNT=%zu TOPOLOGY_VERDICT=%d CAN_DETACH=0 CAN_UNLOCK=0 CAN_FLR=0
evidence.why: the aggregate says how many NVIDIA cards were seen but not selected, which is the peer set the interference question is about

candidates.does_not_prove: that two cards can be actuated in order: the sequence is CPU-side reporting over one immutable snapshot, and B10's memory cost per additional card is untouched by it.

candidates.title: MSI B850 ROM variables
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: Reads the MS-7E56 firmware's `ROM_CMN`/`CSM_CMN` variables and dumps them raw, on the board fingerprint the earlier console analysis was done on. This is the only passive route to the firmware's own display-selection policy; it changes nothing.

evidence.token: MSI_B850_ROM_VARIABLES PLATFORM_FINGERPRINT=MATCH SMBIOS_VERIFIED=0 BIOS_VERSION_VERIFIED=0 GPU_MUTATION=NONE
evidence.why: the probe only runs on the exact board and GPU fingerprint, and it says in the same line that SMBIOS and the BIOS version are not verified

evidence.token: MSI_B850_VARIABLE NAME=%s EFI_STATUS=%#llx BYTES=%zu ATTRS=%#x CAP=%u RAW_ONLY=1 READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: the raw bytes of the variable, with `RAW_ONLY=1`: the firmware's display policy is in there, and the log does not pretend to interpret it

evidence.token: MSI_B850_BDS_POLICY_END NO_VENDOR_CALLBACK=1 NO_LIST_TRAVERSAL=1 NO_GPU_ACTION=1 POOL_UNCERTAIN=%u
evidence.why: the line that bounds the probe: no vendor callback, no list traversal, no GPU action, so the dump cannot have changed the console state it describes

candidates.does_not_prove: which byte is `Initiate Graphic Adapter`, or that clearing it in firmware would give an AMD-exclusive `ConOut`/`ErrOut`: the dump is raw, there is no schema, and nothing here authorises an NVRAM rewrite.

candidates.title: MSI B850 ROM variables with handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The ROM-variable dump plus the pinned Windows handoff, so a passive capture of the firmware's display policy does not end with the operator hunting for a boot entry.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID and does not touch BootOrder

evidence.token: SAVE_LOG_STATUS=%#llx ROTATING_FILE=GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-NNNN.TXT
evidence.why: the dump is written before the handoff, so the evidence survives a handoff that fails

candidates.does_not_prove: anything the base ROM-variable probe does not prove, plus the handoff's own limit: one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: MSI B850 fuse version
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: One 32-bit read of the GSP fuse register per identity-verified card, plus one of the SEC2 register, and nothing else. The only image that reports which firmware signature slot a physical card's fuse selects.

evidence.token: MSI_B850_FWSEC_FUSE GPU=%s STATUS=OBSERVED BAR0_OFFSET=0x8241e0 RAW=%#x LOW16=%#x FUSE_VERSION=%u ARCHIVED_ROM_SIG_MASK=%#x CANDIDATE_SLOT=%u ARCHIVED_SLOT_NONZERO=%u ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
evidence.why: the fuse word and the slot it implies for each card: the per-card half of the Booter/V67/ROM pairing question, and the line ends `ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED`

evidence.token: MSI_B850_FWSEC_FUSE_BEGIN SOURCE=NOVA_CORE_GA102_PLUS READ_ONLY=1 CAN_DETACH=0 CAN_UNLOCK=0 NO_STOP=1 NO_DMA=1 NO_RESET=1
evidence.why: the first line of the probe says it reads only, so it can never establish firmware acceptance: C3 stays where it is whatever the value is

evidence.token: MSI_B850_SEC2_FUSE_BEGIN SOURCE=NOVA_CORE_GA102_PLUS REFERENCE_BOOTER=LINUX_610_43_03 ENGINE_MASK=0x1 UCODE_ID=3 WINDOWS_61742_DESCRIPTOR=UNKNOWN READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: the probe names the reference it decoded against (the Linux 610.43.03 header) and states that the Windows 617.42 descriptor is unknown: the asset-coupling claim, bounded in the log

candidates.does_not_prove: that the slot this fuse names is the slot Windows 617.42 selects; the same line prints `WINDOWS_61742_SIGNATURE_SLOT=UNKNOWN`, and no signature is authenticated anywhere in this path.

candidates.title: MSI B850 fuse version with handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The fuse read plus the pinned Windows handoff: a card that is left alone still has to end the session in Windows, and this is the variant that says so in one boot.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID and does not touch BootOrder

evidence.token: SAVE_LOG_STATUS=%#llx ROTATING_FILE=GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-NNNN.TXT
evidence.why: the fuse reads are written before the handoff begins

candidates.does_not_prove: anything the base fuse probe does not prove, plus the handoff's own limit: one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: MSI B850 SEC2 ucode version
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: One read of the SEC2 version register at BAR0+0x824140 per card, named as the Windows 617.42 register by the Linux 610.43.03 header. It reports a version and refuses to infer a signature from it.

evidence.token: MSI_B850_SEC2_UCODE1 GPU=%s STATUS=OBSERVED BDF=0000:%02x:00.0 BAR0_OFFSET=0x824140 RAW=%#x LOW16=%#x FUSE_VERSION=%u ENGINE_ID=1 UCODE_ID=1 SELECTED_SIGNATURE=UNVERIFIED SECURE_ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: the SEC2 version per card, with the selected signature and the secure-acceptance result stated as unverified in the same line

evidence.token: MSI_B850_SEC2_UCODE1_END READS_SUCCEEDED=%u EXPECTED=2 NO_GPU_WRITES=1 SECURE_ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
evidence.why: the completion line says how many of the expected reads landed and that no GPU write happened: a failed read is visible as a count, not as a silent zero

candidates.does_not_prove: that this version is the one Windows 617.42 uses. The register is named by a Linux header, the log prints `SELECTED_SIGNATURE=UNVERIFIED`, and the Windows signature slot stays `UNKNOWN`.

candidates.title: MSI B850 SEC2 ucode version with handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The SEC2 read plus the pinned Windows handoff, for a bench where the read-only image is expected to return to Windows by itself.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID and does not touch BootOrder

evidence.token: SAVE_LOG_STATUS=%#llx ROTATING_FILE=GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-NNNN.TXT
evidence.why: the read is written before the handoff begins

candidates.does_not_prove: anything the base SEC2 probe does not prove, plus the handoff's own limit: one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: read-only probe of the actuating write set
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: Forty-two BAR0 reads per verified card, at the addresses the waived transaction writes, plus the twenty-four words it reads without writing - the two HwCfg words `falcon_reset()` polls, the RISC-V halt word, the GFW and WPR2 bookkeeping words, and the rest of the set whose refused read stops the transaction. It is the interlock for the first actuation: run the same image before and after, and any block that moved shows up as a different digest. Nothing is written. It also copies the one-megabyte ROM window at BAR0 + 0x300000 and applies the same structural check the transaction applies before it refuses a board.

evidence.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_BEGIN SOURCE=UNLOCK_610_WRITE_SET BLOCKS=%u CONTEXT=%u MODE=READ_ONLY READ_ONLY=1 NO_STOP=1 NO_DMA=1 NO_RESET=1 NO_UNLOCK=1 NO_FLR=1 CAN_DETACH=0 CAN_UNLOCK=0 CAN_FLASH=0 NO_GPU_WRITES=1
evidence.why: the probe declares what it is before it reads anything: a read-only boundary and the size of its own address list, so a run that reads fewer blocks than the table has is visible in the first line rather than by counting the middle.

evidence.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE GPU=%s BDF=0000:%02x:00.0 BLOCK=%s BAR0_OFFSET=%#x ROLE=WRITE STATUS=OBSERVED RAW=%#010x ACCESS=%s READ_ONLY=1 ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
evidence.why: one line per word the actuating sequence writes: block name, the absolute BAR0 address, and the value there before any write exists. Forty-two of them (twenty per engine plus both selectors) is the evidence that this image addresses the same blocks as the transaction. It does not move C5: a readable address identifies the target, and there is no post-state yet to verify.

evidence.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_CARD GPU=%s READ=%u FAILED=%u OBSERVED=%u NOT_ACCESSIBLE=%u WRITE_SET_SHA256=%s DIGEST_CV=CHANGE_DETECTOR_ONLY ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
evidence.why: the per-card digest is labelled a change detector in the line itself, and the line carries the failed-read count beside it: a digest over a partial read set would otherwise look complete. A digest over register values is not firmware acceptance, so C3 stays where it is.

evidence.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_END CARDS=%u BLOCKS=%u CONTEXT=%u EXPECTED_READS=%u READS_SUCCEEDED=%u READS_FAILED=%u DIGESTS=%u NO_GPU_WRITES=1 SECURITY_ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED OBSERVED=%u NOT_ACCESSIBLE=%u
evidence.why: the totals: cards probed, expected reads, reads that landed and reads that did not. A block that does not read back is a number here instead of a silent gap, which is the whole point of probing before the first write.

candidates.does_not_prove: that these are the right addresses for the transaction - only that this image and `src/vendor/unlock_610.c` name the same ones, checked by `tests/test_vram_block_probe.py`, not by the log. A successful read proves the word is reachable through PCI I/O; it does not prove an engine mask, a signature selector or a speed-selector write is permitted on this board, and it cannot say what any value means. The post-actuation half of the comparison has never run, because the actuation has never run.

candidates.title: read-only probe of the actuating write set, with handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The block probe plus the pinned Windows handoff, for a bench where the read-only image has to return to Windows by itself. The end-of-session digest is in the log either way.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID and does not touch BootOrder

evidence.token: SAVE_LOG_STATUS=%#llx ROTATING_FILE=GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-NNNN.TXT
evidence.why: the block lines and the digest are written before the handoff begins, so the evidence survives a handoff that does not

candidates.does_not_prove: anything the plain block probe does not prove, plus the handoff's own limit: one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: preparation for explicit targets, one or both cards
candidates.log: \AD102-UNLOCK\RUNnnnn.TXT, one file per boot, never overwritten
candidates.summary: The active application, built without the waiver: it runs the real inventory and selection, prepares its state, and refuses before `GuInit`. This is the only image here that executes the app's own entrypoint on hardware, which is why it is the one the P gates score. Given both BDFs it does the same thing for two cards in one boot: `GU_ACTIVE_SEQUENCE_PREPARE_ONLY` returns before the `MULTI_TARGET_WITHOUT_WAIVER` check, so preparing an ordered list needs no waiver - executing one does.

evidence.token: ACTIVE_PREPARE=COMPLETE SELECTED=%zu NVIDIA_COUNT=%zu MUTATION_AUTHORIZED=0
evidence.why: the app's inventory, selection and preparation completed on real firmware and the log says mutation was not authorised: the manual loop D5 says does not exist, run once, by hand

evidence.token: LAUNCH_SOURCE DECISION=%s REASON=%s REMOVABLE=%u PARTITION=%u
evidence.why: the app's own launch decision, printed before anything else: the USB-launch requirement observed rather than inferred

evidence.token: BOOT_STATE PRESENT=1 PHASE=%u BOOT_COUNT=%u STATUS=%#llx DEVICE=%04x
evidence.why: the persistent record is read at boot on real firmware, so a later boot's `PRESENT=1` is a record this tree wrote, not a fixture

evidence.token: ACTIVE_PREPARE=SELECTED_UNSUPPORTED_CARD BDF=%04x:%02x:%02x.%u ID=%04x:%04x
evidence.why: building for one BDF and booting with a different card produces this refusal: the negative case of the image-refuses-a-card-it-was-not-built-for rule

evidence.token: ACTIVE_GPU[%zu] BDF=%04x:%02x:%02x.%u ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x CLASS=%04x LEGACY_UNLOCK_DEVICE_ID=%u
evidence.why: the identity the app itself resolved, with the device id it would act on: the first row of a per-SKU entry

evidence.token: ACTIVE_PREPARE=INVENTORIED NVIDIA_COUNT=%zu REQUESTED=%zu READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: how many NVIDIA cards the app saw, and how many of them the build asked for: the two numbers M4's record has to agree with before the ordered list is trusted

evidence.token: ACTIVE_PREPARED_STEP[%zu] BDF=%04x:%02x:%02x.%u ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x LEGACY_UNLOCK_DEVICE_ID=%u READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: one line per selected card, in the order the selection names them: two of them is what a two-card session looks like, and their IDs are what ties each step to silicon

evidence.token: ACTIVE_CONTEXT[%zu]=PREPARED CPU_ONLY=1 MUTATION_AUTHORIZED=0
evidence.why: `PreparePlatformContexts` allocates one platform context per selected card and refuses an alias to the active context or a duplicate pointer, so two of these lines are evidence that two distinct per-card contexts existed at the same time in a read-only build

evidence.token: ACTIVE_REFRESH=PASSIVE_REVALIDATED TARGETS=%zu MUTATION_AUTHORIZED=0
evidence.why: the cards were re-read after preparation and the revalidation passed: the log shows the second observation, not only the first

candidates.does_not_prove: that the ordered list may execute. Preparation and execution are different admissions: executing more than one target requires `-AcceptUnverifiedActuation` (`MULTI_TARGET_WITHOUT_WAIVER` otherwise), and nothing in a preparation log exercises a write, a Stop, a detach, a reset or a FLR. Two prepared contexts prove a list was built, not that a peer card is undisturbed during a mutation - there has never been a mutation.

candidates.title: DXE preparation for explicit targets
candidates.log: \AD102-UNLOCK\RUNnnnn.TXT, one file per boot, never overwritten
candidates.summary: The same preparation as a boot-service driver, loaded from a `Driver####` entry instead of `EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI`. It answers one question the application cannot: whether the same preflight runs under a driver loaded at `ReadyToBoot`.

evidence.token: ACTIVE_EXECUTION=REFUSED REASON=SELECTION_PREPARATION_ONLY BEFORE_GU_INIT=1
evidence.why: both entrypoints call `GuDiscoverSingleGpu`, which refuses there; that shared boundary is what a resident-driver design has to be built on. Neither entrypoint's own banner can print in this build - `ACTIVE_APP=` in `src/app.c` and `ACTIVE_DXE=` in `src/dxe_main.c` both sit behind the `GuDiscoverSingleGpu` success check that refuses

candidates.does_not_prove: that the driver is safe to leave installed, or that `ReadyToBoot` timing is compatible with anything: the catalogue refuses to stage a DXE driver as `BOOTX64.EFI`, so the only path is a `Driver####` entry you add and remove by hand, and that is a firmware change, not a read-only act.

compile-only (`may_be_staged` is false): the image returns before any firmware or GPU operation, and CI already builds it. A boot would add nothing a compile does not already prove.
compile-only, as above: it exists to prove the ordered sources compile together.
compile-only DXE: nothing runs, so there is no log to score.
writes the GPU: this is the `actuate` stage, needs `-AcceptActuatingDeploy`, and is outside a read-only session by definition.
writes the GPU, ordered over several cards: `actuate` stage, and it needs the selection to be exactly what the catalogue says.
writes the GPU from the ESP: `actuate` stage, and it is the only image that could observe B9's ESP-resident half.
writes the GPU with the target chosen at boot: `actuate` stage.
writes the GPU, resident, target at boot: `actuate` stage.
writes the GPU from a driver: `actuate` stage.
writes the GPU, ordered, from a driver: `actuate` stage.

vendor `Stop` on the 3080: `stop-only`, writes the GPU.

readonly_guide.closing: Every candidate above ends at `tools/verify_run_log.py`, and every verdict it prints carries `HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0`. When all of them have been scored, `tools/donor_gate.py --readonly ... --ack M1_...` says whether the session may enter preparation at all; it composes the same verdicts and adds the requirement that every stage saw the same single card. Neither tool, and nothing in this document, turns a captured log into a verified card.

stages.title: Read-only contact
stages.what_it_costs: nothing: the diagnostic never writes a GPU register, resets a Falcon, calls the vendor Stop or loads firmware
stages.exit: the card is enumerated, its BDF and PCI identity are in the log, and the eligibility flags are printed as false
stages.build_note: the read-only image always saves its numbered log; add -WindowsEspGuid '<reviewed GUID>' only if you want the automatic Windows handover

stages.title: Preparation only
stages.what_it_costs: the active app runs its preflight and preparation, logs a refusal before any mutation, and hands back to Windows
stages.exit: preparation completes with MUTATION_AUTHORIZED=0 and no Stop, no waiver and no step line
stages.build_note: a selection without -EnableSingleTargetExecution and without the waiver compiles the preparation-only image (GPU-ACTIVE-PREP-*), which refuses to actuate before it starts

stages.title: Waived actuation
stages.what_it_costs: the one admission that may write: an ordered list executed one card at a time, no retry, with the firmware timer bounded or explicitly off; more than one target is admitted by the same waiver (`MULTI_TARGET_WITHOUT_WAIVER` otherwise)
stages.exit: the waiver is recorded once, the pre-Stop contract is captured, the step reaches a terminal record, and the next boot reads the record it left
stages.build_note: the only waiver switch; it also needs a reviewed local/boot_profile.h or -RuntimeEsp, and the matched assets on the ESP. `-SelectionBdfs 'a,b'` builds the ordered two-card list, and the step lines then carry `ORDER=`/`TARGET=` indexes into it

gates.title: the read-only image ran

requires.token: GPU TOPOLOGY DIAGNOSTIC ONLY - no GPU hardware writes or unlock calls
requires.why: the banner is printed before any observation, so its presence is the cheapest proof that this build and not another one ran

forbids.why: a read-only session must not contain the waiver admission, which only the actuating build prints
the Stop contract is captured inside the release path; its presence means a Stop was attempted, which no read-only run does

gates.proves: the read-only diagnostic started and wrote its own log
gates.does_not_prove: that the enumeration below finished, or anything about the card

gates.title: the inventory finished, and the collector said so

requires.why: the strict collector reports how many protocol handles it included and excluded, which is the shape of the enumeration it actually performed

the NVIDIA owner inventory ran, and it runs only on the strict collector's success branch (`if(pci_ok)`): the failure branch prints `NVIDIA_DRIVER_OWNER_INVENTORY=UNAVAILABLE PCI_CAPTURE_FAILED=1` instead. This line therefore proves the walk completed without a vendor callback, and that the driver images' provenance is unverified
the report reached its own last line. A log that stops earlier - a hang, a reset, an aborted save - cannot satisfy R2, which is the case a truncated capture fails on

forbids.why: any enumeration failure, at any stage, invalidates the inventory even when later lines look complete
the GOP census is part of the inventory; a failed capture makes every per-GPU GOP count in the log meaningless

gates.proves: the strict PCI walk completed and reported its scope, the NVIDIA owner inventory ran on its success branch, the GOP census did not fail, and the report reached its last line
gates.does_not_prove: that every PCI node was read correctly or that the topology is usable: a handle that was excluded is counted rather than described, and the supplementary observation that would cross-check it exists only on the failure path

gates.title: at least one NVIDIA card is named

requires_any.why: the driver-owner line carries BDF, driver binding and opener state for one card
the active-app inventory line carries BDF and PCI identity for one card

gates.proves: the run is about a real card with an address and an identity, not an empty machine
gates.does_not_prove: that the identity matches the donor card the operator recorded by hand

gates.title: the block probe read every word the transaction writes

only_if.why: the gate scores one optional image: it applies only to a boot whose log carries the block probe's own opening line, and is NOT_APPLICABLE - never PASS - in any other boot

requires.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_BEGIN SOURCE=UNLOCK_610_WRITE_SET BLOCKS=%u CONTEXT=%u MODE=READ_ONLY READ_ONLY=1 NO_STOP=1 NO_DMA=1 NO_RESET=1 NO_UNLOCK=1 NO_FLR=1 CAN_DETACH=0 CAN_UNLOCK=0 CAN_FLASH=0 NO_GPU_WRITES=1
requires.why: the probe says what it is once per boot and states the size of its own address list: a second copy would mean two cards' worth of output in one bracket

requires.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE GPU=%s BDF=0000:%02x:00.0 BLOCK=%s BAR0_OFFSET=%#x ROLE=WRITE STATUS=OBSERVED RAW=%#010x
requires.why: at least forty-two observed write-set words: twenty per engine plus both selectors, which is the whole table. Fewer means a block did not read back and the interlock is incomplete

requires.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_END CARDS=%u BLOCKS=%u CONTEXT=%u EXPECTED_READS=%u READS_SUCCEEDED=%u READS_FAILED=%u DIGESTS=%u NO_GPU_WRITES=1 SECURITY_ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
requires.why: the closing line carries the arithmetic: cards, blocks, expected reads, reads that landed and reads that did not. `READS_FAILED=0` and `READS_SUCCEEDED=EXPECTED_READS` are what make the block list complete rather than partial

forbids.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE GPU=%s BDF=0000:%02x:00.0 BLOCK=%s BAR0_OFFSET=%#x ROLE=WRITE STATUS=UNAVAILABLE
forbids.why: a word the probe could not read is a hole in the interlock: the address was never confirmed on this silicon, so the stage does not pass
the probe withholds its digest when any read failed; a log that says so has no before-and-after comparison to offer

gates.proves: that a read-only image reached every BAR0 word the actuating sequence writes, on each verified card, before anything wrote to them. That is the interlock: the address list is not a surprise at actuation time
gates.does_not_prove: that the values are right, that a selector write will be accepted, or that the transaction will unlock anything. Reading a register before writing it identifies the block and nothing more; the post-actuation half of the comparison needs an actuation, and none has run

gates.title: the probe read the ROM window the transaction refuses a board on

only_if.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_END CARDS=%u BLOCKS=%u CONTEXT=%u EXPECTED_READS=%u READS_SUCCEEDED=%u READS_FAILED=%u DIGESTS=%u NO_GPU_WRITES=1 SECURITY_ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED OBSERVED=%u NOT_ACCESSIBLE=%u ROMS=%u
only_if.why: a log whose closing line carries the ROM count was written by a build that reads the ROM window; a log from before that build is NOT_APPLICABLE rather than silently passing

requires.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_ROM GPU=%s BAR0_OFFSET=0x300000 BYTES=%u SIGNATURE=0x%04x PCIR_OFFSET=0x%04x PCIR_VENDOR=0x%04x PCIR_DEVICE=0x%04x LIVE_DEVICE=0x%04x MATCH=%u SHA256=%s READ_ONLY=1 ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
requires.why: one structural readout per verified card: the ROM's own signature, its PCIR offset and identity, the live device id and whether they name the same card. Two cards are the bench, so two lines

forbids.why: a window the probe could not copy is the exact read the transaction makes before it writes, and it did not happen: the stage cannot claim the ROM is a candidate for this board

gates.proves: that a read-only image copied the megabyte at BAR0 + 0x300000 the transaction copies before its first write, and that the image's own signature and PCIR identity name the card it was read from
gates.does_not_prove: that the ROM is authentic, that it carries the FWSEC-FRTS descriptor the transaction looks for, or that preparation will accept it. A MATCH=1 says the structure names this device and nothing more; SIGNATURE_AUTHENTICATED is not printed because nothing here authenticates a signature

gates.title: the ROM window the probe read is in a file a later build can parse

only_if.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_ROM_FILE GPU=%s BYTES=%u FILE=%s SHA256=%s ROLE=PARSE_OFFLINE READ_ONLY=1 ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
only_if.why: a log with no capture line came from an image that only hashed the window; that boot is NOT_APPLICABLE rather than silently passing, and a run of the capturing build cannot look like one of the hashing one

requires.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_ROM_FILE GPU=%s BYTES=%u FILE=%s SHA256=%s ROLE=PARSE_OFFLINE READ_ONLY=1 ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
requires.why: one file per verified card, each line carrying the digest of the megabyte that was copied, so the bytes that produced the digest left the machine and a parser can be run against them off the bench

forbids.why: the window was read and hashed but no file was written, and a digest on its own cannot answer the FWSEC question the transaction asks before its first write

gates.proves: that a read-only image put the megabyte it copied from BAR0 + 0x300000 into a file on its own volume, named after the card it came from and the run that captured it, with the digest printed on the same line as the file name
gates.does_not_prove: that the file holds any particular descriptor, that the ROM is authentic, or that the FWSEC-FRTS descriptor the transaction looks for is present and acceptable. Nothing in the image parses a descriptor; the file is the input to that question, not an answer to it

gates.title: the fuse word that selects a packed signature was read
gates.proves: that a read-only image read the sixteen-word fuse window at BAR0 + 0x8241c0 and, for each card it verified, printed the word ucode id 9 addresses together with the version gpu_unlock_fuse_version() computes from it - the number unlock_transaction_fwsec() turns into a packed-signature slot before pci_set_master() and before its first write
gates.does_not_prove: that the word will read the same at transaction time, that the version selects a packed signature that is present in the ROM, or that the selected signature authenticates. A fuse word is a value read once through PCI I/O; nothing here verifies a signature, and the slot question stays open until the version is compared with each ROM's sig_versions mask - 0x3 for the 4090 and 0x7 for the 3080 in the captured set, both of which include version zero

requires.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_FUSE_END GPU=%s BDF=0000:%02x:00.0 BASE=%#x WORDS=%u READ=%u FAILED=%u UCODE9_OFFSET=%#x UCODE9_RAW=%#010x UCODE9_VERSION=%u UCODE9_ACCESS=%s UCODE9_UNREAD=0 READ_ONLY=1 NO_GPU_WRITES=1
requires.why: one closing line per verified card, each naming the word ucode id 9 addresses, its value, and the version that value implies: two cards are the bench, so two lines, and a card whose word is missing says UCODE9_UNREAD=1 instead of being absent

forbids.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_FUSE_WINDOW_UNREADABLE GPU=%s BDF=0000:%02x:00.0 BASE=%#x WORDS=%u FAILED=%u READ_ONLY=1
forbids.why: the window was addressed and not one of its words came back: the read that would have answered the slot question did not happen, so the stage cannot claim it did
a word inside the window refused the PCI read - and that word may be the one the transaction's ucode id addresses. A partial window is a partial answer
the closing line reports that the word this run was after did not come back, so the version printed beside it is a placeholder and not what the transaction would compute

only_if.why: a log with no per-word fuse line - in either its value form or its refused form - was written by an image that does not read the window. That boot is NOT_APPLICABLE rather than silently passing, so a run of the earlier image cannot look like one of the reading build. The marker is the address and the ucode id, which both forms print, so a window that refused every word still counts as an attempt and is scored by the forbids below

gates.title: the app refused to actuate and said so first

requires.why: the refusal is printed inside `GuDiscoverSingleGpu` before any GU init, and it is the line that bounds the session. The application's own `ACTIVE_APP=PREPARATION_ONLY` banner sits *after* that call returns success, and the preparation image is refused *by* that call, so the banner is unreachable in exactly the build it describes; P1 required it until the first two physical preparation runs showed no preparation image can print it. The same holds for the DXE entrypoint's `ACTIVE_DXE=PREPARATION_ONLY` banner
preparation reached its end with mutation explicitly unauthorized

forbids.why: a step that may write must not appear in a preparation session
no Stop may be attempted in a preparation session

gates.proves: the image refused to actuate at the discovery boundary, before any GU init, and the preflight ran to completion with mutation still unauthorized
gates.does_not_prove: that the refusal is the right one for these cards, or that preparing a list means the list may execute: it says the entrypoint is a preparation entrypoint. The counts say what was selected, not what was safe

requires_any.token: BOOT_STATE PRESENT=1 PHASE=%u BOOT_COUNT=%u STATUS=%#llx DEVICE=%04x
requires_any.why: a record from an earlier boot was found and decoded
no record was found, which is the correct state for the first boot on a wiped machine

gates.proves: the record path works on this machine, in one of its two honest states
gates.does_not_prove: that the record can be written, or that it survives a power loss; that needs a run that is interrupted

gates.title: the waiver is in this boot's log, exactly once

requires.why: the waiver is a boot-level decision: more than one occurrence means a retry or a second entrypoint, which the plan forbids

forbids.why: a simulator run prints SIMULATED instead of WAIVED_UNVERIFIED; if both appear the log is not a clean hardware record

gates.proves: an actuating image reached its admission exactly once
gates.does_not_prove: that the admission was safe; the waiver is the reason it is not

gates.title: the pre-Stop capture exists and names what it is missing

requires.token: STOP_CONTRACT device=%04x stage=%zu OWNER=%d COLD=%d CONSOLE=%d PEERS=%d
requires.why: the capture names the device, the stage and the four observations that just held; the rest of the line is the requirements
the same line ends with the decision and the missing set, so a capture that found nothing missing cannot be confused with one that did

gates.proves: the image captured its pre-Stop state and stated which requirements it cannot establish
gates.does_not_prove: that any of the six unobservable facts hold - by construction they are the ones this image cannot see

requires.why: the only line printed immediately before a card may be written

gates.proves: an ordered step was admitted after every preflight
gates.does_not_prove: how the step ended; that is the next gate

gates.title: the step reached a terminal record instead of the log ending

requires_any.why: the step completed and peer state was re-observed
the coordinator halted deliberately and promised no successor; this is a legitimate ending, not a failure

requires_any.token: STOP: stage=%s status=%#llx mutated=%u retained=%u fault=%u
requires_any.why: the application recorded the transaction result, including whether the card was mutated, retained or faulted

gates.proves: the log ends at a decision the image recorded itself, so truncation is distinguishable from an ending
gates.does_not_prove: that the ending was a good one; HALTED passes this gate on purpose

requires.token: BOOT_STATE PRESENT=1 PHASE=%u BOOT_COUNT=%u STATUS=%#llx DEVICE=%04x
requires.why: the state that is supposed to survive a failed boot is only proved by a boot that comes after it

gates.proves: the record survived whatever the actuation did, and a later boot could read it
gates.does_not_prove: that the record was correct, or that the machine came back warm rather than through a power cycle

advisories.why: the application prints whether the firmware timer is armed or deliberately off. The DXE entrypoint does not print this, so it is a note rather than a gate
every boot now records where it started from and, when it refuses, which gate failed
says whether a bundle was ever staged on the stick, before discovery assumes anything about assets

advisories.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_REFUSED GPU=%s WORDS=%u OF=%u SIGNATURE=0xbadf0000 ACCESS=NOT_ACCESSIBLE
advisories.why: the probe met words inside the actuating write set that the engine returns its own inaccessible() shape for: the read succeeded at the PCI I/O level and the value is not device state. Printed once per card that has any, so a run cannot look fully observed while part of the write set was refused

printed by `ReportPciEvidence`, which runs only when the strict collector failed (`if(!pci_ok)` in `GuTopoDiagnosticMain`). A healthy run does not print it, so its presence in a log is a finding to explain - and gate R2 required it until the first physical run showed that no healthy machine can satisfy that

the probe's ROM read did not produce a structural readout: the header word was not a ROM signature, or the megabyte copy failed. Printed with a REASON= field, once per card, so an unreadable window is a line in the log instead of a missing one

manual_gates.title: the physical recovery path is on the bench before the first run
manual_gates.why: an external programmer and a known-good firmware image are the only way back from a card that no longer answers; they cannot be fetched afterwards
manual_gates.record: the programmer model, the image digest, and the SPI flash part number, noted in the session log

manual_gates.title: the donor card's identity is written down before the run
manual_gates.why: the log will name a BDF and a device ID; without the card's serial and the slot it was in, those cannot be tied to a piece of silicon afterwards
manual_gates.record: serial number, slot, board model, the VBIOS version the vendor tool reports

manual_gates.title: the log medium starts empty
manual_gates.why: RUN0001.TXT must be this boot, or a stale file is indistinguishable from a live one and the gate verdicts describe the wrong run
manual_gates.record: a directory listing of the stick before the boot, photographed or copied

manual_gates.title: every card in the machine is recorded, and the ordered target list is written down before the image is built
manual_gates.why: this fork executes an ordered list rather than a single card: one card is active at a time, each step is gated on its predecessor's completion record, and the cards that are not the current target are tracked for drift rather than ignored. A log names BDFs and device IDs; only the operator can tie those to serials and slots, and only the operator can say which card the session is meant to reach and in what order
manual_gates.record: for every NVIDIA card in the machine: serial, slot, board model and the VBIOS version the vendor tool reports; then the ordered BDF list the image was built with, in the order the session intends to execute

manual_gates.title: a HALTED step ends the day, not the loop
manual_gates.why: no retry is a property of the image; re-running after a halt is the operator reintroducing the risk the image refused
manual_gates.record: the halt line, and the decision to stop, in the session log

manual_gates.title: Windows is started normally with the card enumerated after every run
manual_gates.why: the log cannot see Windows; device start, driver binding and a display output have to be observed by a person
manual_gates.record: the Windows build, the driver version, and the device status in Device Manager

never_established_by_a_log.why: no code in this tree observes the Windows 617.42 Booter; the comparison is external evidence that has to be produced separately and has never been produced
the Stop contract's TARGET_GOP requirement is never observed - the image does not read the target's firmware GOP ownership
the contract's LOG requirement needs the log closed before the Stop; the image cannot close the file it is writing to
no recovery procedure has been executed on this card, so the requirement stays false no matter what the log shows
the vendor Stop callback has no measured worst-case duration; a log line that shows it returned says nothing about how long it could take
the contract's DMA requirement is not observable here; bus-master state is checked, engine idleness is not
the log ends at the handover; whether Windows started the device is only visible in Windows
a benchmark number is a measurement on a machine, not a property of this source
the state after cutting power mid-transaction has never been observed, and a clean run says nothing about it

go_no_go.summary: One stage's gates passing is not permission to run the next stage. This tool composes the stage verdicts into a single go/no-go answer and is the only thing in the repository that does so.
rules: the read-only stage must pass before preparation counts as done, and preparation must pass before actuation may be attempted at all

every stage must identify the same ordered target list: the list the first stage names (`SELECTION_REQUEST[n]`, `ACTIVE_PREPARED_STEP[n]`, `PASSIVE_SELECTION=`) must be the list every later stage names, in the same order, every card in it must appear in the read-only census, no card may appear twice, and the PCI id printed beside each BDF must agree across stages. A session where no stage names a target and the machine has more than one card is refused rather than guessed at: an ordered list of two cards is a normal session in this fork, an unnamed one is not
every manual gate must be acknowledged by its exact id; an unknown id is refused, so a typo cannot silently stand in for M6
a log carrying the fixture marker is refused (exit 3) unless --self-test is given, and a GO from a self-test still prints SYNTHETIC=1
go_no_go.verdict: `DONOR_GATE VERDICT=GO NEXT=...` with every line carrying `HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0`; anything else prints `VERDICT=NO_GO` and one `BLOCKED` line per reason
exit_codes: 3 the log set is synthetic and --self-test was not given
go_no_go.does_not_prove: that any stage behaved as its gates say, or that the card is safe: a GO repeats evidence the operator supplied, it does not create any

captured_runs.title: Captured runs, scored
captured_runs.note: Physical runs, stored as files and scored by the same tool an operator runs. Each entry pins the digest of the stored log, the facts quoted from it, and the verdict line the verifier prints for it, and `tests/test_hardware_session.py` re-scores the file on every run: the record cannot drift from the evidence, and a gate that no healthy machine can satisfy fails the suite instead of the operator. The read-only runs and the preparation runs are scored per stage; `tools/donor_gate.py` is what composes them into a go/no-go answer.

runs.history: First run of the block probe, and the first read-only image here that reads the transaction's own address list. It answers the question it was built for: 88 of 88 reads landed on both cards, so the forty-two words `src/vendor/unlock_610.c` writes are all addressable through PCI I/O on this machine. It also found something the plan did not have. On both cards the five falcon-bridge words read as state, while the rest of the SEC2 window - and, on the 4090, nearly all of the GSP window as well - returns `0xbadf5620`, which is the shape `inaccessible()` treats as a refused read: 45 of the 84 write-set words across the two cards. The probe as built printed those as `STATUS=OBSERVED`, so section 11.33 teaches it to classify them, adds the two `HwCfg` words `falcon_reset()` polls before its first write, and records the finding here.

It reads through the same `Mem.Read` call with the same width and bar index (`src/port.c`'s `GuRead32For`), so the values should reproduce, but that image has never run. It does not say why the engine refuses those words, or how a run would lift the refusal; and `0x8400f4`, the word `falcon_reset()` polls first, was not in the probed set, so whether the transaction stops at that poll or gets as far as its first write is still open.

runs.history: The read-set build of the probe. -0006 answered whether the words the transaction writes are addressable; this run answers whether the words it reads are readable, and with it the question -0006 left open: falcon_reset()'s first poll, 0x8400f4, reads 0x67b7 on the 4090 and 0x47f7 on the 3080, both as state. With bit 31 clear the pre-reset wait is the tolerated timeout the code's own comment describes, and with bit 12 clear the post-reset release wait is satisfied by the value that was already in the register, so it does not demonstrate that a reset happened. Two of the twenty-four new words are refused: SEC2.IRQSTAT on both cards, which only log_falcon_state() reads, and the 4090's GSP.RISCV halt word. Everything the layout and entry gates demand by exact value is present on both cards - PLM 0xffffff8f, GFW.PLM 0x8b8f, GFW.BOOT 0x3ff, GSP.CPUCTL 0x10, WPR2 high 0 - and the sixty-six write-set words are unchanged from -0006, digest included.
runs.does_not_show: that either card can be actuated. The probe reads and never resets, so the two refused words have no cause attached, and whether a refused word is refused again after an engine reset is exactly what only an actuating run can say. Nothing here touches the ROM window at BAR0+0x300000, which is the first content gate the transaction passes through, nor the profile and entry-selector bookkeeping the entry gate also requires. `ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED` stands: a word that reads as state is not a signature check.

runs.history: The first boot of the ROM-window build, and the run that caught this probe's own defect. Both cards returned a ROM header (0xaa55) and a PCIR structure at 0x0170 carrying NVIDIA's vendor id and a device id naming the card - 10de:2684 on the 4090, 10de:220a on the 3080, both matching the GPU lines in the same log - so the structural check the transaction applies is satisfied on this bench. The probe still reported MATCH=0 because it passed pci_id & 0xffff, the vendor, as the live device id. The ROM was never the problem; the comparison was handed the wrong half of the identity. Fixed to pci_id>>16, with a test that pins the split against the PCI printer's own %04x:%04x encoding.
runs.does_not_show: that a fixed build reads MATCH=1 on these cards - that needs the re-run. Nor does it show that the ROM carries the FWSEC-FRTS descriptor preparation parses from the same megabyte, or that GuAd104Prepare accepts the board on its other terms: assets, selector stability, and the reference policy that is compiled out. MATCH says the structure names the device and nothing more; no signature is authenticated here.

runs.history: The defect §11.37 found is fixed here and the boot was repeated, so this run answers two questions at once: MATCH=1 on both cards, and the two PROM files whose digests match the lines that describe them. The images themselves were parsed off the bench by tests/test_fwsec_v2.c and the result is recorded in `prom_captures`: both carry a version-3 FWSEC-FRTS descriptor with a non-zero ucode id and 384 bytes per signature, which is what GuAd104FwsecMatches() requires.
runs.does_not_show: that the files are authentic firmware (SIGNATURE_AUTHENTICATED=0 on every line), or that the signature slot the fuse word selects exists for either card: the transaction reads BAR0 0x8241e0 for ucode 9 and that word has never been read on this bench. The 1 MiB images are NVIDIA firmware and are not stored here, only their digests and the fields the parser reported.

runs.history: The boot §11.40 asked for. Sixteen words per card at BAR0 0x8241c0, printed with the version gpu_unlock_fuse_version() computes, and gate R7 scores the read. The read set the probe already covered is unchanged - the fuse window is not part of it, which is why the totals are the same as -0008 and -0009 - and the sixteen extra reads are the only new ones.

observations.why: the same word on the 3080 reads 0x00000003 - version 2 - and its mask 0x7 contains bit 2, so it would copy the third of three. Both cards are selectable, which is the question this boot existed to answer

runs.does_not_show: that either fuse word reads the same when the transaction reads it, that the signature the version selects is the one the driver will accept, or that any signature authenticates (SIGNATURE_AUTHENTICATED=0 stands). It also does not answer the two questions that remain before a first write: which captured PROM reference the image trusts, and whether a staged asset bundle matches the pinned hashes.

prom_captures.note: The files the -0009 boot wrote and what the transaction's own parser reported for each. The 1 MiB NVIDIA firmware images are NOT stored in this repository: the digest in the stored log and the digest here tie the record to the bytes, and tests/test_vram_block_probe.py holds the parsed fields to the conditions GuAd104FwsecMatches() applies.
prom_captures.parser: tests/test_fwsec_v2.c in file mode: gpu_unlock_vbios_fwsec() from src/vendor/vbios_610.c walks the image, and the admission bits are the four conditions of GuAd104FwsecMatches() in src/profile.c

fuse_captures.note: The fuse window -0009 left unread, as -0010 reported it. The word the transaction uses is the one its ROM's ucode id names; both captured ROMs say 9, so the row that matters is the ninth. The window is kept whole because the tail is not uniform: on the 4090 the id-15 and id-16 words read 0x7fff, which is version 15 and selectable by neither mask. A probe that read one word and assumed would be reporting an assumption, not a measurement.
fuse_captures.does_not_show: that these words are stable across boots or across a driver load, or that the selected packed signature authenticates. The fuse is read, not latched; a second boot that reads the same word is a repeat, not a proof of stability.
